title: Eraser: interior erased holes REFILL on any planar rebuild — interactive eraser drag inside a fill loses its trail (only the last stamp stays erased)
description:
VERIFIED with repro. The planar read-back <-> rebuild round trip is NOT idempotent for shapes with interior holes, and the interactive eraser chains rebuilds per pointermove, so erasing inside a fill visibly re-fills the trail behind the cursor.

ROOT CAUSE: planarShapeToShape (packages/core/src/engine/planar/query.ts:346+) emits an interior hole as a closed loop path CARRYING the surrounding fill (all loops of a component share the Fill object; rendering relies on nonzero winding to cut the hole). But buildArrangementFromShapes' assignFaceFillsBySampling (packages/core/src/engine/planar/build.ts:67-114) treats EVERY closed filled path as an independent covering region with last-covering-wins sampling — no winding/parity. The outer silhouette polygon covers the hole area, so on ANY rebuild the hole face resolves to the fill again.

REPROS (all confirmed by direct kernel calls on origin/main b4430b6):
1. INTERACTIVE ERASER TRAIL: sq = red rect 0..200x0..100; chain per-move segments exactly like StageArea.tsx:3170-3263 does (planarEraseShape(cur, buildEraserStamp([prev,cur],8)) with cur = previous result): after 3 increments along y=50, point (50,50) (first segment's center) covers with winding count 1 = REFILLED; only the last stamp (90,50) still reads as a hole (count 2). Real Flash 8: the whole swept trail stays erased.
2. ERASE THEN DRAW: erase a disk hole at (50,50) inside a 100x100 red square, then planarMergeCommit a small blue rect overlapping the square's corner (any overlapping commit pulls the shape through the kernel; bbox-cull only hides this for DISJOINT commits) -> merged read-back covers (50,50) with count 1: the hole is refilled red in the rendered doc.
3. PICKING: livePlanarShape/locateFace on the post-erase shape reports fill=red at the hole center, so paint bucket / selection / faucet see a phantom fill where the user erased.

WHY IT MATTERS: this makes the vector eraser (docs/03/04, Flash 8 true vector subtraction) unusable for interior erasing — the most common eraser gesture (scrub inside a fill) self-reverts while dragging. It also silently corrupts erased artwork on the NEXT overlapping draw.

SUGGESTED FIX (kernel-adjacent, but concretely reproduced as required): make fill-region sampling winding-aware — group fillRegions by source shape + Fill identity and use even-odd/nonzero parity ACROSS the group (brushpaint.ts pointInShapeFill already does exactly this for the ribbon guard), OR mark emitted hole loops (e.g. holeOf/fill-less with explicit region role) so build.ts subtracts them. Must keep the oracle suite green (merge-drawing-oracle.spec.ts diff=0) and planar-eraser.test.ts intact.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) round-trip idempotence unit test: for a shape with an interior hole, planarShapeToShape(buildArrangementFromShapes([s])) preserves hole coverage parity at the hole centroid; (b) chained 3-increment erase (repro 1) leaves ALL three stamp centers erased; (c) erase-then-overlapping-commit (repro 2) keeps the hole; (d) existing planar/eraser/merge tests + oracles pass.

Related: 1327 (even-odd pointInEraser union — different spot, same even-odd family), 1399 (Erase-Inside fill-index keying), 1335 (read-back accumulation). Found by brush/eraser Flash-8 fidelity audit.
